The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a high degree of spatial variation in regolith thickness that cannot be explained by the typical controls on regolith thickness, namely weathering and erosion, and that the controls on regolith development are more local than previously thought.
regolith thickness is not a simple function of topographic position, but is a more complex function of lithology, structure and vegetation.

regolith thickness in the Ouachitas does not conform to the expectations of equilibrium models, and the local variations are not well correlated to slope, aspect, elevation, or other variables that are commonly used to explain variation in thickness of regolith in the Ouachitias or elsewhere.
